gloss: to omit; to leave out reluctantly

definitions.gloss: to omit; to leave out reluctantly; to cut for brevity
definitions.explanation: To reluctantly leave something out, typically due to time or space constraints. Implies that the omitted content has value and the speaker regrets not being able to include it.

examples.japanese: {詳細|しょうさい}は{割愛|かつあい}します。
{時間|じかん}の{都合|つごう}で{一部|いちぶ}{割愛|かつあい}させていただきます。
examples.english: Due to time constraints, I will have to leave some parts out.

examples.japanese: {紹介|しょうかい}したいことはたくさんあるが、{紙面|しめん}の{関係|かんけい}で{割愛|かつあい}する。
examples.english: There's a lot I'd like to introduce, but I'll have to leave it out due to limited space.

notes:
Originally meant to part reluctantly with something one loves ({愛|あい} = love, {割|か}つ = to cut). The modern usage retains this nuance of reluctant omission — you would include the content if you could, but constraints prevent it. Very common in presentations, speeches, and written articles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {説明|せつめい}を{割愛|かつあい}する: to omit the explanation
- {詳細|しょうさい}は{割愛|かつあい}: details omitted
- {紙面|しめん}の{都合|つごう}で{割愛|かつあい}: omitted due to space constraints
- {時間|じかん}の{都合|つごう}で{割愛|かつあい}: omitted due to time constraints

USAGE:
This is a formal, polite way to tell an audience or reader that you are skipping something. Using {割愛|かつあい} signals respect for both the omitted content and the audience. It is a staple of academic presentations, business meetings, and journalistic writing.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {省略|しょうりゃく}する: to abbreviate, to omit — more neutral; no connotation of reluctance
- {省|はぶ}く: to cut, to leave out — more casual and direct
